q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is August 15, 2026. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release would typically occur in late August or early September 2026 (approximately 2-3 weeks away). The question asks about the *forward guidance* that will be announced at that earnings release, which is imminent.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research provides NVIDIA's explicit forward guidance for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**.

This guidance was already announced on May 20, 2026, as part of their Q1 FY2027 earnings report. The question is asking what this guidance will be in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release itself, which creates a logical issue: the company has already provided this guidance publicly.

**Key facts from the research:**
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion (up 85% YoY)
- Q2 FY2027 forward guidance (announced May 20, 2026): $91.0 billion ± 2%
- This represents approximately 12% sequential growth from Q1 to Q2
- Guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue
- This beat the LSEG average estimate of $86.84 billion

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 forward guidance (for Q3) announced at the Q2 earnings release will be close to $91.0 billion, though companies sometimes adjust guidance between quarters based on current business trends.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

1. **Weakening demand signals** - If NVIDIA observes softening demand in AI infrastructure post Q1, they might lower forward guidance
2. **Stronger-than-expected competition** - If competitive products gain traction, forward guidance could be reduced
3. **Macro headwinds** - Economic slowdown affecting customer capex spend
4. **Inventory corrections** - If customers work through existing inventory faster than expected
5. **Geopolitical risks** - Further China export restrictions could impact overall guidance trajectory
6. **Conservative guidance philosophy** - Management might lower guidance to ensure achievement

## (d) What would push the value higher?

1. **Accelerating AI demand** - If enterprise and cloud providers are accelerating AI infrastructure buildout beyond expectations
2. **China revenue inclusion** - Though unlikely given current export controls, any relaxation could add upside
3. **Market share gains** - If NVIDIA takes share from competitors faster than expected
4. **Product cycle benefits** - New product launches or architectural improvements driving higher ASPs
5. **Macro strength** - Strong enterprise capex spending supporting higher bookings
6. **Full quarter data** - By the time of Q2 earnings (likely late August/early September), NVIDIA will have ~2+ months of Q2 actuals, reducing uncertainty

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**From the research provided:**
- Q1 FY2027 revenue: $81.6 billion (actual)
- Q2 FY2027 forward guidance: $91.0 billion ± 2% (announced May 20, 2026)
- Sequential growth implied: ~12% Q1 to Q2

**Historical growth pattern:** The research notes Q1 revenue was up 85% YoY, with data center revenue up 92% YoY, indicating sustained hypergrowth.

No reliable base rate for typical guidance revisions between announcement and earnings is available in the provided research.

---

## Reasoning

The critical insight here is that NVIDIA has **already publicly announced** its Q2 FY2027 forward guidance on May 20, 2026, at the time of the Q1 earnings release. This guidance was $91.0 billion ± 2%, which translates to a range of $89.2B to $92.8B.

When companies provide forward guidance early in a quarter (as NVIDIA did for Q2 on May 20), they typically maintain or slightly adjust that guidance at the next earnings call, unless significant business developments warrant a change. By late August/early September when Q2 earnings are reported, NVIDIA will have high visibility into most of Q2 performance.

The most probable scenarios:
1. **~70% probability:** Guidance remains at or very close to $91.0B ± 2% (the already-announced figure)
2. **~20% probability:** Slight upward adjustment to $92-94B range (accelerating momentum)
3. **~10% probability:** Downward adjustment to $88-90B range (demand softening)

Given the range provided (99.5B to 115.5B) appears to be broader than necessary, and the already-announced guidance sits well below this range, my median estimate centers on the announced figure with modest consideration for potential positive revisions given the momentum evident in Q1 results.

The guidance of $91.0B ± 2% represents approximately 12% sequential growth from Q1's $81.6B, which appears reasonable for a company experiencing 85% YoY growth in a hypergrowth phase.

q_45367.research_text: NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue was released on May 20, 2026, as part of their Q1 FY2027 earnings report. The company expects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This guidance is significantly above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion by LSEG [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). NVIDIA explicitly stated that this outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), which was up 85% year-over-year [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), driven by a 92% increase in data center revenue [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report).
